entities.summary: Murad II was the second sultan of the Ottoman Empire, ruling from 1421 to 1444 and again from 1446 to 1451, after the death of his half-brother Mehmed I. His reign was marked by the Ottoman conquest of much of Southeastern Europe and the Balkans, including the city of Kosovo, which became a symbol of Ottoman power. The Ottomans also continued their expansion into the Middle East and North Africa, further solidifying their position as a dominant world power. In 1451, Murad II defeated the Serbian army at the Battle of Varna, securing Ottoman control over the region. This victory marked the beginning of Ottoman expansion into Eastern Europe, setting the stage for the empire's eventual rise to dominance. Murad II's legacy as a skilled military leader and administrator helped to cement the Ottoman Empire's place in history as one of the greatest empires of all time.
